meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

выходить.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to get out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выйти'.

examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

examples.text: Но он же выходит в туалет, на кухню.
examples.trans: But he goes out to the bathroom, to the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Grab him!
It needs a wash.
Four-eyes! Grab him!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'a little; nearly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I nearly fell.
Wait a little.

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to kill', paired with 'убивать'.

examples.trans: Do you want to kill me?
I'll kill you! (said in anger)

examples.text: Ты смотришь на меня так, как будто убить хочешь.
examples.trans: You look at me as if you want to kill me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine there.
Who's there?
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ходу').

examples.trans: Looks like your plan worked.
That's just like him!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my own', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'key' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Give me the keys.
Where's the key?
The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'jacket, coat' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Put the jacket on.

examples.text: На улице холодно, возьми тёплую куртку.
examples.trans: It's cold outside, take a warm jacket.

examples.text: Карамельно-сливочный цвет. Очень тебе к лицу! Надень куртку.
examples.trans: A caramel-cream colour. It really suits you! Put the jacket on.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'would keep, would leave'.

examples.text: Вика, ну он одинокий. Я же не оставлю его одного.
examples.trans: Vika, come on, he's all alone. I can't just leave him on his own.

examples.text: Я же не оставлю его одного.
examples.trans: I can't just leave him on his own.

examples.text: Ты что, голову в Москве оставил?
examples.trans: What, did you leave your head in Moscow?

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to quarrel, to swear', paired with 'поругаться'.

examples.trans: Let's not fight.

examples.text: Давай не будем ругаться при детях.
examples.trans: Let's not fight in front of the children.
The neighbors often quarrel over trifles.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be ill', paired with 'заболеть'.

examples.trans: My mother is ill.
Your son is ill.

examples.text: Я этого не хочу. Но вспомни, у тебя сын болеет.
examples.trans: I don't want that. But remember, your son is ill.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('warm').

examples.trans: And where are your warm gloves?

examples.text: Да, его тёплая шапка лежит прямо здесь.
examples.trans: Yes, his warm hat is lying right here.

examples.text: Снимайте скорее с него тёплые валенки.
examples.trans: Take off his warm felt boots quickly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'лица'). Common feminine noun meaning 'street; outside' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are reporters out on the street!
It is cold outside.

examples.text: Там на улице журналисты! Они меня ждут!
examples.trans: There are reporters out on the street! They're waiting for me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: And let them build their shopping centres.
Let him say it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ъезд'). Common masculine noun meaning 'entrance, doorway' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They were standing near the entrance.

examples.text: Просто постояли у подъезда и быстро уехали.
examples.trans: They just stood near the entrance and quickly left.
Moved to live in the hallway.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: А ты иди на биржу труда. Там есть работа.
examples.trans: You go to the job centre. There's work there.

нельзя.gloss: it is not allowed; one can't

meanings.en: it is not allowed; one can't
meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'льзя').

examples.trans: Not allowed? All right.
You can't smoke here.
Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'претить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forbid, to ban', paired with 'запрещать'.

examples.trans: But Anikeev forbade it!
The doctor forbade him to drink.

examples.text: Аникеев же запретил! Нам нельзя пить.
examples.trans: But Anikeev forbade it! We mustn't drink.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning '(to) home, homeward', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.
It's time to go home.

examples.text: Так, мы идём к слепым. А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'носить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bring', paired with 'принести'.

examples.trans: Our organization offers its apologies.

examples.text: Я приношу бутылку шампанского и свечи.
examples.trans: I'll bring a bottle of champagne and candles.

examples.text: И не надо больше никаких документов сюда приносить!
examples.trans: And don't bring any more documents in here!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'allergy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'm allergic to cats.
He's allergic to caviar.

examples.text: Мама говорила, что у меня на икру аллергия.
examples.trans: Mum said I'm allergic to caviar.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.trans: I don't know.
As you all know...

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

собираться.gloss: to intend, to be about to; to gather

meanings.en: to intend, to be about to; to gather
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обираться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to intend, to be about to; to gather', paired with 'собраться'.

examples.trans: I am planning to move.

examples.text: Ну и что? Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: So what? I'm planning to move anyway.
I'm planning to move anyway.

выгнать.gloss: to kick out, to evict, to drive out

meanings.en: to kick out, to evict, to drive out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'гнать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to kick out, to evict, to drive out', paired with 'выгонять'.

examples.trans: She will kick me out!

examples.text: Для тебя она добрая. А меня она выгонит!
examples.trans: She's kind to you. But she'll kick me out!

examples.text: Значит, меня не выгонят со службы?
examples.trans: Does that mean I won't be fired from service?
